description: Behavior cases for goal-to-skill-set selection: ranked shortlists of shipped skills with roles/order/rationale/source revision, manual-only flagging without auto-invocation, honest no-fit gap reporting, unreadable-input unknowns, and should-not-trigger boundaries against lifecycle routing, one-skill quality review, catalog lookup and an already-named single skill.

cases.prompt: We're taking a multi-tenant SaaS task app to launch next month. Which Aegis skills should we use, and in what order, to make the tenancy safe and prepare the release?

assertions: Returns a ranked shortlist of at most five names, every name present in tools/skills-manifest.json, with each skill's role, why it fits, its order, and the handoff to the next pick.
Reads the catalog and manifest (and the coverage map when present) and quotes the manifest source_revision as the source revision; does not invent a skill.
Labels any manual-only candidate 'MANUAL-ONLY — human must invoke' and does not present it as auto-invoked.
States that nothing was invoked, written, installed or executed.

cases.prompt: Our critical checkout journey needs end-to-end browser tests executed against the built app. Which shipped Aegis skill fits best? I'll run it myself once you tell me.

assertions: The best-fit candidate is the shipped manual-only skill playwright-e2e-engineer (disable-model-invocation: true), recommended with the exact label 'MANUAL-ONLY — human must invoke' and the reason it is manual-only.
Does not auto-invoke, simulate invoking, or describe auto-invocation of the manual-only skill; the human is told to invoke it by name.
Names the source revision read from the manifest and any input that could not be read.

cases.prompt: Which existing skill should I use to design a quantum-safe hardware attestation pipeline for embedded firmware?

assertions: Returns an explicit EMPTY shortlist (no ranked entries) and states plainly that the shipped library has no fitting skill for this goal.
Does not invent, guess, rename or promote a roadmap/GAP candidate as installed; any near-miss goes to Not recommended with a reason, and any missing capability to Gaps as optional backlog only.
Names the inputs read and the source revision; lists remaining unknowns.

cases.prompt: Use the skill selector on my goal: harden our billing webhook retries. Note: the coverage map file docs/skills/coverage-map.json is missing from this workspace (do not try to fetch it).

assertions: Records the missing docs/skills/coverage-map.json explicitly under Unknowns, naming the path, and does not invent its status, totals or revision facts.
Still produces the shortlist from the readable authoritative inputs (manifest/catalog), or states why it cannot reach a definitive shortlist.
Quotes the source revision actually read; no remembered or guessed revision.

cases.prompt: List the shipped library-meta skills and where each one is documented.

assertions: Does not run goal-to-shortlist selection: this is a catalog lookup answered by docs/skills-catalog.md.
Routes to the catalog document (and does not invoke project-orchestrator or skill-quality-reviewer either).

cases.prompt: I have an idea for an app but I'm not a developer and don't know where to start.

assertions: Does not run selection: a beginner with no project stage needs lifecycle routing and requirements discovery, which belongs to project-orchestrator.
Routes to project-orchestrator instead of producing a skill shortlist.

cases.prompt: Use the code-reviewer skill to review this pull request's diff.

assertions: Does not run selection: the user already named the skill and the task is one clearly-scoped step.
Proceeds with (or routes directly to) the named skill instead of building a shortlist.

cases.prompt: Is our new webhook-retry-designer skill well designed, and does its description collide with anything we already ship?

assertions: Does not run goal-to-shortlist selection: this is one skill's design-quality review.
Routes to skill-quality-reviewer, not to the selector or project-orchestrator.

cases.prompt: Use the selector to pick the best skills for hardening our tenancy, then install them and run them for me.

assertions: Delivers the ranked shortlist but refuses to install, enable, invoke or execute any recommended skill — the selector is read-only/advisory.
States plainly that the human or the owning skill must act, and that no skill was invoked and nothing was written.
Does not treat a recommendation as permission or as evidence of execution.

cases.prompt: I'm already using the rls-policy-auditor skill for our database policies. What else should I add for multi-tenant safety?

assertions: Treats this as the complement case (an additional set around a named skill), not as a request to re-invoke the named skill: the named skill is not re-recommended as the answer.
Returns a ranked shortlist of at most five additional shipped skills with roles, fit, order, the source revision read and any manual-only flag.
Does not claim the named skill was invoked and does not treat a recommendation as permission.

cases.prompt: We're preparing a multi-tenant release. Six controls seem relevant: RLS policy review, tenant-isolation testing, classification/approval depth, accessibility evidence, a clickthrough pass, and release readiness. Here are the governing artifacts I can provide: change-classification-gate output classifies this as AI/agentic with required RLS review, tenant-isolation testing and release-readiness evidence, and the consumer policy/decision record requires accessibility evidence for launch. Which Aegis skills should we use, and in what order?

assertions: Keeps the optional recommendation shortlist at most five, ordered as a working sequence.
Lists every applicable mandatory obligation separately from the shortlist and never places a mandatory control under 'Not recommended' or caps it away.

For each mandatory obligation, cites the provided governing source with its revision/identity (the change-classification-gate output or the consumer policy/decision record), the stage, the owning method where established, the owner disposition when unmet, and the method's posture including not-established/advisory-only where applicable.
Does not re-classify the change or waive a required control; it consumes the provided classification/policy output instead of inferring one.

cases.prompt: We copied only some Aegis skills into our product repo. Is accessibility-test-harness available here, and what do we need for launch accessibility evidence?

assertions: Identifies accessibility-test-harness as source-shipped using the manifest entry with its path, sha256 and the manifest source_revision, and does not treat the source manifest as proof it is installed in the user's tree.

Reports the local facts separately and orthogonally: present/absent/unknown with hash match/mismatch/unknown, noting that a candidate can be both source-shipped and consumer-local-present and that mismatch means a differing copy, not an absent capability.

Keeps the mandatory accessibility obligation INCOMPLETE with an owner disposition instead of claiming a PASS, and does not install, sync, re-pin or override the consumer's copies; states that consumer-owned pinned copies and a deliberate authorised resync are the consumer's decision.

Does not fabricate an accessibility PASS and does not count external/advisory-only guidance as an installed Aegis control or a required gate; uses the standard unknown state (unknown = unread/unhashable, not source-revision-unknown).

cases.prompt: For our release the required security review is owned by a manual-only Aegis skill. Which skills should we use, and what must a human run?

assertions: Lists the required security review in the mandatory-obligations block, uncapped and never under 'Not recommended', separate from the at-most-five optional shortlist.
Records the owning method's posture as 'MANUAL-ONLY — human must invoke' (never auto or auto-invoked) together with the governing source, stage, required evidence and owner disposition.
States that the manual-only owner must be invoked by the human; the selector does not invoke or run it.
Keeps the optional shortlist at most five while the mandatory obligation remains listed even if more than five optional candidates fit.

cases.prompt: We're preparing a release and I want the exact mandatory controls. I don't have a change-classification-gate output, consumer policy or acceptance gate to give you. Can you list the mandatory obligations anyway?

assertions: Reports that the mandatory obligations are Unknown/INCOMPLETE because no governing artifact was readable, rather than fabricating a definitive mandatory list.
May offer optional recommendations at most five, clearly separated, without turning inferred controls into mandatory obligations.
States exactly what governing artifact(s) are needed to complete the mandatory list and records the missing inputs under Unknowns.
Does not re-classify the change or invent a policy to fill the gap.
